title: Bounded owned-browser teardown: proxied SSE upstreams end with their browser connection
user_story: Deterministic browser acceptance finishes promptly and reliably instead of depending on a 30s upstream socket timeout racing a 30s finish limit.

requirements.description: After finish the owned browser process exits within 10 seconds; journeys keep every existing oracle check.
When the browser-side connection closes, the proxied upstream request to the owned application is destroyed; origin allowlist, 30s upstream bound and error mapping unchanged.

nonfunctional: No timeout or assertion relaxation; a stricter 10s teardown assertion is added
Original pr/all failure, its raw evidence and the repair ledger entry are preserved
outputs: Owned browser exits promptly after evidence and trace are written
preconditions: Built frontend, Node, Chromium; disposable owned application server
acceptance_criteria: RED: both deterministic journeys exceed 10s teardown (~29s)
GREEN: both PASS with teardown below 10s

scenarios.expected: Workflow journey PASS with prompt teardown
Closed browser connections do not leave upstream SSE requests open
Teardown strictly below 10s, far from the 30s finish limit
Controlled-fault journey keeps its fault oracle and still tears down promptly

recovery: Revert the two-line proxy change; the stricter assertion would then fail visibly. TASK-UAT-TEARDOWN-6513 max three cycles.
test_environment: REAL_LOCAL owned server, Chromium persistent context and loopback proxy in disposable data; no model.

review.method: Same-agent root-cause review from phase timestamps (trace at +0.1s, exit at +29s) and proxy code; not independent.

tdd.scope: Actual REAL_LOCAL browser runs before and after the proxy change.
